title: Clearance Rack Two-Step
subject: a man who buys cowboy boots off the clearance rack for a Saturday dance and can't peel the bright orange $39.99 sticker off the sole, so every spin on the floor shows the whole room what he paid
caption: Neotraditional honky-tonk, 90s-style dancehall country. Twangy Telecaster chicken-pickin' fills, crying pedal steel swells, double-stop fiddle answering each line, walking upright bass, brushed shuffle drums with a snappy snare. Dry live-band mix with slapback echo on the vocal. Male baritone with a warm Texas drawl, deadpan and winking. 118 BPM, G major. Rowdy, sly and grinning. No trap hi-hats, no autotune, no arena rock guitars, no pop synths, no hip-hop beat.
lyrics:
[Intro - Telecaster and fiddle]

[Verse 1]
Found 'em on the bottom shelf
Ostrich brown and almost new
Thirty-nine and ninety-nine
Bright orange on the left shoe

[Chorus]
Every time I spin her round
That sticker winks at the crowd
Clearance rack two-step
I'm cheap and I'm proud

[Verse 2]
Tried my thumbnail, tried a key
Tried a little gasoline
Now the whole floor knows my price
Every turn they read it clean

[Chorus]
Every time I dip her low
Back row starts to read out loud
Clearance rack two-step
I'm cheap and I'm proud

[Bridge - fiddle break]
She just laughed and leaned in close
Said her dress was half price too

[Chorus]
So spin me, darlin', spin me round
Show 'em both our tags right now
Clearance rack two-step
We're cheap and we're proud

[Outro - pedal steel tag]
Thirty-nine and ninety-nine
Best money I spent all year
